# API reference

All namespaces are `AchReactive`.

## DataBase\<T>

```csharp
public sealed class DataBase<T> where T : IData
{
    void Load(IDataLoader<T> loader);   // full replace
    void Add(IDataLoader<T> loader);    // merge
    void Add(T item);
    T Get(string id);
    bool TryGet(string id, out T value);
    bool Has(string id);
    void Clear();
    int Count { get; }
    IReadOnlyCollection<T> All { get; }
}
```

## IDataLoader / implementations

```csharp
public interface IDataLoader<T> where T : IData
{
    IReadOnlyList<T> Load();
}

public sealed class JsonDataLoader<T> : IDataLoader<T> where T : IData
{
    JsonDataLoader(string json, JsonSerializerSettings settings = null);
    JsonDataLoader(Func<string> read, JsonSerializerSettings settings = null);
}

public sealed class CsvDataLoader<T> : IDataLoader<T> where T : IData
{
    CsvDataLoader(string csv, ICsvMapper<T> mapper);
    CsvDataLoader(Func<string> read, ICsvMapper<T> mapper);
}

public interface ICsvMapper<out T> where T : IData
{
    T Map(IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> row);
}
```

## Data model

```csharp
public interface IData { string Id { get; } }

[Serializable]
public class EntityData : IData
{
    public string id;
    public Dictionary<string, float> stats;
    public Reaction[] reactions;
    public string Id => id;
}

[Serializable]
public class Reaction
{
    public string trigger;
    public ParamBag triggerParams;
    public ConditionDef[] conditions;
    public EffectDef[] effects;
}

[Serializable] public class EffectDef    { public string type; public ParamBag @params; }
[Serializable] public class ConditionDef { public string type; public ParamBag @params; }
```

## ParamBag

```csharp
public sealed class ParamBag
{
    static readonly ParamBag Empty;
    bool Has(string key);
    T Get<T>(string key, T fallback = default);
    bool TryGet<T>(string key, out T value);
    void Set<T>(string key, T value);
}
```

## ReactionEngine

```csharp
public sealed class ReactionEngine
{
    int Run(string trigger, EntityData data, ReactionContext ctx);
}

public sealed class ReactionContext
{
    public IEntity Source;
    public IEntity Target;
    public IReadOnlyList<IEntity> Targets;
    public IWorld World;
    public ParamBag Params;
}
```

## Registry

```csharp
public delegate void EffectFn(ReactionContext ctx);
public delegate bool ConditionFn(ReactionContext ctx);
public delegate bool TriggerFn(ReactionContext ctx, ParamBag triggerParams);

public static class EffectRegistry
{
    static void AutoRegister();
    static void Register(string name, EffectFn fn);
    static bool TryGet(string name, out EffectFn fn);
    static bool Has(string name);
    static IEnumerable<string> Names { get; }
}
// ConditionRegistry and TriggerRegistry follow the same pattern
```

## Integration boundary

```csharp
public interface IEntity
{
    string Id { get; }
    Vector3 Position { get; set; }
    StatSheet Stats { get; }
    bool IsAlive { get; }
}

public interface IWorld
{
    IEntity Spawn(string dataId, Vector3 at);
    void Collect(Vector3 center, float radius, List<IEntity> buffer);
}
```

## StatSheet / CooldownStore

```csharp
public sealed class StatSheet
{
    void SetBase(string statKey, float value);
    float GetBase(string statKey);
    float Get(string statKey);   // final value with modifiers applied
    void AddModifier(string statKey, string modifierType, float value, object source);
    void RemoveSource(object source);
}

public sealed class CooldownStore
{
    CooldownStore(Func<float> timeProvider = null);
    bool IsReady(string id);
    void Start(string id, float cooldown);
    float Remaining(string id);
}
```

# Changelog

## 0.1.0

First public release. Transitioned from the skill-only tool (Skill Creator) to the **domain-agnostic reaction framework AchReactive**.

### Added

- **Data Layer** — `IData`, `IDataLoader<T>`, `DataBase<T>` (no use of typeof)
- **Loader** — `JsonDataLoader<T>` (Newtonsoft), `CsvDataLoader<T>` + `ICsvMapper<T>`
- **Reaction Layer** — `Reaction`, `EntityData`, `ParamBag`, `ReactionContext`, `ReactionEngine`
- **Registry** — `Effect/Condition/TriggerRegistry` (attribute auto-collection + manual registration)
- **Default behavior pool** — 8 effects, 8 conditions, 1 trigger guard
- **Integration boundary** — `IEntity`, `IWorld`, `StatSheet`, `CooldownStore`
- **UIToolkit authoring tools** — Type Designer (code generation), Data Editor (data generation)
- **Basic sample** — example with two domains: skills + monsters

### Changed

- Package name `com.achieve.skill-creator` → `com.achieve.reactive`
- Namespace → `AchReactive`
- `JsonUtility` → `Newtonsoft.Json` (wrapper classes removed)

### Removed

- Skill-only legacy (`SkillSystem`/`SkillRunner`/`EffectExecutor`, etc.)
- The buff duration/stack system is temporarily on hold because it requires a redesign of runtime state (planned for a follow-up)

# Getting started

## Installation

In the Unity Package Manager, choose **Add package from git URL** and enter the following address.

```
https://github.com/achieveonepark/AchReactive.git
```

Or add it directly to `Packages/manifest.json`.

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "com.achieve.reactive": "https://github.com/achieveonepark/AchReactive.git"
  }
}
```

The requirement is **Unity 2021.3 or later**. The only dependency is `com.unity.nuget.newtonsoft-json`,
which is installed automatically.

## 1. Implement the integration boundary

AchReactive does not impose a structure on your game. You only need to implement two interfaces.

- `IEntity` — the subject/target of a reaction (characters, monsters, etc.)
- `IWorld` — the world boundary for spawning, range queries, etc.

```csharp
using AchReactive;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class Character : MonoBehaviour, IEntity
{
    public StatSheet Stats { get; } = new StatSheet();   // provided by the package, use as is
    public string Id => name;
    public Vector3 Position { get => transform.position; set => transform.position = value; }
    public bool IsAlive => Stats.GetBase(StatKeys.Hp) > 0f;

    void Awake()
    {
        Stats.SetBase(StatKeys.Hp, 100f);
        Stats.SetBase(StatKeys.HpMax, 100f);
        Stats.SetBase(StatKeys.Atk, 10f);
        Stats.SetBase(StatKeys.Def, 2f);
    }
}
```

## 2. Author the data

Define skills as JSON in the `reactions` format. (You can also build them with the [Data Editor](/AchReactive/en/usage/authoring-tools.md) instead of writing them by hand.)

```json
[
  {
    "id": "fire_slash",
    "cooldown": 5.0,
    "reactions": [
      {
        "trigger": "on_use",
        "conditions": [{ "type": "alive" }],
        "effects": [
          { "type": "damage", "params": { "power": 1.8 } },
          { "type": "log", "params": { "message": "fire_slash 명중!" } }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

## 3. Assemble and run

```csharp
using AchReactive;

var skills = new DataBase<SkillData>();
var engine = new ReactionEngine();

void Start()
{
    // Auto-collect the behavior pool (includes default damage/heal/…)
    EffectRegistry.AutoRegister();
    ConditionRegistry.AutoRegister();
    TriggerRegistry.AutoRegister();

    // Load data — any source you like
    skills.Load(new JsonDataLoader<SkillData>(() => skillsJson.text));
}

void UseSkill(IEntity caster, IEntity target)
{
    var ctx = new ReactionContext { Source = caster, Target = target };
    engine.Run("on_use", skills.Get("fire_slash"), ctx);
}
```

Default effects like `damage`, `heal`, and `add_modifier` are provided by the package, so no extra code is required.
You can immediately see a working scene in the **Basic** example under `Samples`.

## Next steps

- [Concepts](/AchReactive/en/usage/concepts.md) — why the structure is this way
- [Default behavior pool](/AchReactive/en/usage/reactions.md) — the list of provided effects/conditions
- [Extending](/AchReactive/en/usage/extending.md) — new behaviors and new domains

# AchReactive

**AchReactive** is a Unity framework that builds all game content — skills, monsters, items, maps, quests, and more —
from data composition following the **trigger → condition → effect** pattern.

## Core idea

> Domains are infinite, but behaviors (primitives) are finite.

Building a new system for every domain means filling in the `domain × behavior` matrix each time.
AchReactive makes the behavior pool **shared by all domains**, turning this multiplication into addition.
From the second domain onward, it's almost free.

```
        damage  heal  add_modifier  spawn
Skill     ✓      ✓        ✓
Monster                    ✓          ✓     ← reuse the same effect
Item               ✓       ✓
```

## Features

- **Domain-agnostic** — a single `DataBase<T>` handles Skill/Monster/Item/… all of them
- **Source-agnostic** — load from anywhere: JSON, CSV, remote, etc. (implement `IDataLoader<T>` for a new source)
- **Automatic behavior registration** — collects `[Effect]`/`[Condition]`/`[Trigger]` methods via reflection, zero wiring
- **UIToolkit authoring tools** — create types and data in the editor (no hand-written JSON)
- **Minimal dependencies** — just Newtonsoft.Json

## At a glance

```csharp
// 1) Auto-collect the behavior pool (includes default effects/conditions/triggers)
EffectRegistry.AutoRegister();
ConditionRegistry.AutoRegister();
TriggerRegistry.AutoRegister();

// 2) Load data (any source)
var skills = new DataBase<SkillData>();
skills.Load(new JsonDataLoader<SkillData>(() => json));

// 3) Run — identical even across domains
engine.Run("on_use", skills.Get("fire_slash"), ctx);
```

## Next steps

- [Getting started](/AchReactive/en/getting-started.md) — from installation to running your first reaction
- [Concepts](/AchReactive/en/usage/concepts.md) — triggers/conditions/effects and the domain model
- [Extending](/AchReactive/en/usage/extending.md) — adding new behaviors and new domains

# Authoring tools

You don't write data by hand in JSON. Two UIToolkit editor windows generate code and data.

## Type Designer — generate code from a type

Menu: **Tools ▸ AchReactive ▸ Type Designer**

```
Type Name:   [ Monster        ]
Base Type:   [ EntityData ▾   ]
Output:      [ Assets/Generated ]
Fields:
  [ hp        ] [ Float    ▾ ] [−]
  [ dropTable ] [ StringArray ▾ ] [−]
  [ + Add Field ]
                              [ Generate ]
```

Pressing **Generate** produces two files.

- `MonsterData.cs` — an `IData` implementation that inherits `EntityData` (Newtonsoft compatible)
- `MonsterCsvMapper.cs` — an `ICsvMapper<MonsterData>` implementation

Supported field types: `string`, `int`, `float`, `bool`, and their array forms (`string[]`, etc.).
Arrays are separated by `|` in CSV.

If you'd rather not generate, writing `class MonsterData : EntityData { ... }` by hand works 100% as well.

## Data Editor — create/edit data

Menu: **Tools ▸ AchReactive ▸ Data Editor**

- Left: instance list (add with + Instance)
- Right: the selected instance's `id` and the **Reactions builder**
  - **Trigger** dropdown — registered triggers + common channels (on_use, on_hit …)
  - **Conditions / Effects** — `type` is a dropdown populated from the registry, `params` is JSON
- Top **Export JSON…** — save as a `reactions`-format array

```
Reactions
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Trigger: [ on_use ▾ ]              [−]  │
 │ Conditions (AND)                        │
 │   [ alive ▾ ] [ {} ]              [−]   │
 │   [ + Condition ]                       │
 │ Effects                                 │
 │   [ damage ▾ ] [ { "power": 1.8 } ] [−] │
 │   [ + Effect ]                          │
 └────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The key point is that **you don't type trigger/condition/effect types directly**.
The dropdowns expose only the names actually registered in the registry, so typos and unregistered types are blocked at the source.
The saved JSON is read by `JsonDataLoader` as is.

> Authoring is UI, runtime consumption is data files — users never need to touch JSON directly.

# Core concepts

## Multiplication into addition

Building a dedicated system for each domain (SkillSystem, MonsterSystem, …) means
filling in the `domain × behavior` matrix every time. AchReactive makes the **behavior pool
shared by all domains**, turning this into `domain + behavior`.

- Adding a new domain → 1 data class (0 system code)
- Reusing an existing behavior → 0 code, data only
- A genuinely new behavior → 1 function, then shared by all domains

## The four layers

```
Data Layer       IData · IDataLoader<T> · DataBase<T>      (generic, provided by the package)
Reaction Layer   Reaction · ReactionEngine · Registry      (generic, provided by the package)
Behavior Pool    [Effect("damage")] [Condition("alive")]   (written by the game, domain-agnostic)
Domain Data      SkillData · MonsterData · ItemData         (data, code-gen capable)
```

The top two layers are provided by the package and don't change. You only fill in the bottom two layers.

## Reaction = trigger → condition → effect

Every domain is expressed in the same language.

```
Reaction
 ├─ trigger      "on_use" | "on_hit" | "on_hp_below" ...
 ├─ conditions   evaluated with AND (alive, hp_below, chance ...)
 └─ effects      executed in order (damage, heal, add_modifier ...)
```

The shape is identical even across different domains.

```json
// Skill — damage on use
{ "trigger": "on_use",
  "effects": [{ "type": "damage", "params": { "power": 1.8 } }] }

// Monster — enrage when HP is at or below 30%
{ "trigger": "on_hp_below", "triggerParams": { "threshold": 0.3 },
  "effects": [{ "type": "add_modifier", "params": { "stat": "atk", "modifier": "percent_add", "value": 0.5 } }] }

// Item — aura on equip
{ "trigger": "on_equip",
  "effects": [{ "type": "add_modifier", "params": { "stat": "def", "modifier": "flat", "value": 5 } }] }
```

`add_modifier` is **one and the same code** whether a skill or an item uses it.

## Integration boundary

The game only implements two interfaces.

- **`IEntity`** — `Id`, `Position`, `Stats` (StatSheet), `IsAlive`
- **`IWorld`** — `Spawn`, `Collect`

Effects/conditions access `Source`/`Target`/`Targets`/`World` through the `ReactionContext`.

## We don't use typeof

When grouping multiple domains, we don't use a type-keyed service locator like `Dictionary<Type, object>`.
Each `DataBase<T>` is **held explicitly**, and effects that need cross-domain references are
solved with [manual registration + closure capture](/AchReactive/en/usage/extending.md#cross-domain).

```csharp
public sealed class GameDataContext
{
    public readonly DataBase<SkillData>   Skills   = new();
    public readonly DataBase<MonsterData> Monsters = new();
}
```

# Data and sources

## IData and DataBase

All domain data implements `IData` (= `string Id`). `DataBase<T>` is an in-memory index of
`id → definition`, and **all domains share this single class generically**.

```csharp
var skills = new DataBase<SkillData>();
skills.Load(loader);              // full replace
skills.Add(loader);               // merge
SkillData s = skills.Get("fire_slash");
bool has   = skills.Has("fire_slash");
```

## Source-agnostic — IDataLoader\<T>

No matter where you read data from, it goes through the same boundary, `IDataLoader<T>`. The package provides two implementations.

### JSON

Based on Newtonsoft.Json, it reads a top-level array as is. (No wrapper class needed.)

```csharp
// Direct string
skills.Load(new JsonDataLoader<SkillData>(json));

// Deferred read (file/StreamingAssets/network)
skills.Load(new JsonDataLoader<SkillData>(
    () => File.ReadAllText(path)));
```

```json
[
  { "id": "fire_slash", "cooldown": 5.0, "reactions": [ /* ... */ ] }
]
```

### CSV

Uses the first row as the header and converts each row with `ICsvMapper<T>`. Quotes, commas, and newlines are supported.

```csharp
skills.Load(new CsvDataLoader<SkillData>(
    () => File.ReadAllText(path), new SkillCsvMapper()));
```

`ICsvMapper<T>` implementations are usually generated by the [Type Designer](/AchReactive/en/usage/authoring-tools.md).

### Custom sources

For binary, ScriptableObject, in-house formats, etc., you only need to implement `IDataLoader<T>`.

```csharp
public sealed class MyBinaryLoader<T> : IDataLoader<T> where T : IData
{
    public IReadOnlyList<T> Load() { /* decode directly */ }
}
```

> JSON in the editor, CSV/Remote in production — you just **swap out the source**.

## Data format (reactions)

Domain data inherits from `EntityData`. The common fields are `id`, `stats`, and `reactions`.

```csharp
[Serializable]
public class SkillData : EntityData   // inherits id / stats / reactions
{
    public float cooldown;
    public float castTime;
}
```

```json
{
  "id": "fire_slash",
  "cooldown": 5.0,
  "stats": { "manaCost": 20 },
  "reactions": [
    {
      "trigger": "on_use",
      "conditions": [{ "type": "alive" }],
      "effects": [{ "type": "damage", "params": { "power": 1.8 } }]
    }
  ]
}
```

`params` is an arbitrary key-value (`ParamBag`) that effects/conditions read with type conversion,
like `ctx.Params.Get<float>("power")`.

# Extending

## Adding a new behavior

### Path A — Attribute (recommended)

Write a static method annotated with `[Effect]`/`[Condition]`/`[Trigger]`, and `AutoRegister()`
collects it automatically from all assemblies. There is no wiring code.

```csharp
using AchReactive;

public static class MyEffects
{
    [Effect("teleport")]
    public static void Teleport(ReactionContext c) =>
        c.Source.Position = c.World != null ? /* ... */ c.Source.Position;
}
```

The signatures are fixed.

```csharp
[Effect("name")]    static void M(ReactionContext ctx)
[Condition("name")] static bool M(ReactionContext ctx)
[Trigger("name")]   static bool M(ReactionContext ctx, ParamBag triggerParams)
```

### Path B — Manual registration

Use this when you need DI, runtime state, or closures.

```csharp
EffectRegistry.Register("teleport", c => myTeleporter.Move(c.Source));
```

## Adding a new domain

A new domain needs only **1 data class**. There is no system code.

```csharp
[Serializable]
public class MonsterData : EntityData   // inherits id / stats / reactions
{
    public int expReward;               // domain-specific field
}
```

```csharp
var monsters = new DataBase<MonsterData>();
monsters.Load(new JsonDataLoader<MonsterData>(() => json));

engine.Run("on_hp_below", monsters.Get("goblin_boss"), ctx);
```

`damage`/`add_modifier`, etc., reuse what skills already registered, as is → 0 lines of code.
Data classes and CSV mappers can be generated with the [Type Designer](/AchReactive/en/usage/authoring-tools.md).

## Cross-domain

When an effect needs to reference another domain's data, use **manual registration + closure capture**
instead of auto-registration to capture the relevant `DataBase<T>`. No type keys (typeof) are used.

```csharp
var items = new DataBase<ItemData>();

EffectRegistry.Register("drop_item", c =>
{
    var item = items.Get(c.Params.Get<string>("itemId")); // capture items via closure
    c.World.Spawn(item.id, c.Source.Position);
});
```

> Recommendation: auto-register only pure behaviors that know nothing about domains; manually register only effects that need domain coupling.

## AOT (IL2CPP) caveat

`AutoRegister()` is reflection-based, so methods may be stripped in IL2CPP builds.
Preserve the assembly containing your behavior methods with `link.xml`.

```xml
<linker>
  <assembly fullname="YourGameAssembly" preserve="all" />
</linker>
```

If you want to avoid reflection, you may use only **Path B (manual registration)**.

# Reactions and default behaviors

## Execution flow

```csharp
var engine = new ReactionEngine();
engine.Run("on_use", skillData, ctx);
```

`Run(trigger, data, ctx)` iterates over `data.reactions` and processes each reaction as follows.

```
1. Does the trigger channel name match?      (otherwise skip)
2. Does the trigger guard pass?              (TriggerRegistry, passes if none)
3. Do all conditions (AND) pass?             (ConditionRegistry)
4. Execute effects in order                  (EffectRegistry)
```

The return value is the number of reactions actually executed.

## ReactionContext

```csharp
var ctx = new ReactionContext
{
    Source  = caster,     // subject
    Target  = target,     // single target
    Targets = targets,    // area targets (takes priority if present)
    World   = world,      // spawn/query boundary
};
```

An effect reads its own arguments from `ctx.Params`. The engine injects them per item.

## Default effects

| type              | Description                                 | params                                |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `damage`          | reduces hp by `atk*power + flat - def`      | `power`, `flat`                       |
| `heal`            | heals `atk*power + flat` (capped at hp_max) | `power`, `flat`                       |
| `set_stat`        | set a stat base value                       | `stat`, `value`                       |
| `add_stat`        | increase/decrease a stat base value         | `stat`, `delta`                       |
| `add_modifier`    | add a stat modifier (basic buff form)       | `stat`, `modifier`, `value`, `source` |
| `remove_modifier` | remove modifiers for a source token         | `source`                              |
| `spawn`           | spawn an entity via World                   | `entityId`                            |
| `log`             | debug log                                   | `message`                             |

The `modifier` value is one of `flat` / `percent_add` / `percent_mul`. The targets are all of `Targets` if present,
otherwise `Target`.

## Default conditions

| type                        | Description          | params          |
| --------------------------- | -------------------- | --------------- |
| `always`                    | always true          | —               |
| `alive` / `dead`            | target alive/dead    | —               |
| `chance`                    | pass by probability  | `value` (0\~1)  |
| `hp_below` / `hp_above`     | compare HP ratio     | `value` (0\~1)  |
| `stat_above` / `stat_below` | compare a stat value | `stat`, `value` |

Unless otherwise specified, conditions evaluate `Target` (or `Source` if absent).

## Default trigger guard

Most triggers (`on_use`, `on_hit`, `on_equip`, etc.) fire on the channel name alone, so they have no guard.
Only triggers that need a threshold comparison have a guard.

| type          | Description                                                | triggerParams      |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `on_hp_below` | fires only when Source's HP ratio is at or below threshold | `threshold` (0\~1) |

## Stat conventions

The default effects/conditions use the following keys (`StatKeys`). To use a different scheme, register the effect
directly to override it.

| Key      | Meaning                                           |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `hp`     | current health (resource)                         |
| `hp_max` | maximum health (denominator for ratio conditions) |
| `atk`    | attack power (modifiers applied)                  |
| `def`    | defense (modifiers applied)                       |
